SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Rounders, part of Creating and Executing in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: How do the fielding skills help players in a Rounders game?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Rounders together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: The learner talks, shares materials and ideas on executing the skill of batting, fielding

when playing rounders.

● Creativity and imagination: The learner works with peers and exchange new ideas to inspire creativity when carving the

bat.

Values:
● Social justice: The learner shares rounders bats equally and takes turns to bat and play a Rounders game.

● Love: The learner portrays a caring attitude while executing and playing the Rounders game.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Safety and security- The learner becomes more aware of safety procedures as they participate in Rounders game.

● Social cohesion: The learner collaborates in discussing the skills of rounders and carving a rounders bat.

21

Link to other learning areas:

Mathematics: The learner acquires concepts of order and counting while practising fielding and batting.
